exports.name: InitializeTest
exports.signature: (*sanctumConcurrency) InitializeTest(ctx context.Context, payload models.ConcurrencyRequest, logger lumber.Logger) (bool, error)
exports.description:
InitializeTest : This function is called before attempting allocation of device. It performs the following actions
1. Generate Intent based on testType & isPrivateCloud
2. Use Sanctum SDK to initialize the test and lock concurrency

Success response from this function indicates that the state of test is marked
as initialized on sanctum side.

Parameters
----------
testID: testID generated by Sanctum Service
testType: type of test like app automation, web automation etc.
orgID: organization_id of the user who triggered the test
userID: user_id of the user who triggered the test
isPrivateCloud: is test is to be executed on dedicated device
logger: Global logging object

as initialized on sanctum side.

----------
testID: testID generated by Sanctum Service
testType: type of test like app automation, web automation etc.
orgID: organization_id of the user who triggered the test
userID: user_id of the user who triggered the test
isPrivateCloud: is test is to be executed on dedicated device
enqueue: this param is used to set the state of test as queued on the sanctum side
logger: Global logging object

architecture.overview: Repository with 229 files across 61 modules. 1952 public exports, 387 types, 1352 functions.

ai_analysis.pattern: Layered microservice architecture with domain-driven design elements

layers.name: Presentation Layer
layers.purpose: Handle HTTP requests, WebSocket connections, and API endpoints

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.purpose: Business logic orchestration and application services

layers.name: Domain Layer
layers.purpose: Core business entities and domain logic

ai_analysis.data_flow: Requests flow from controllers through services to repositories, with domain models representing core entities. External integrations communicate through dedicated service modules (lmms, lums, etc.). Kafka handles asynchronous messaging, Redis provides caching, and WebSocket enables real-time communication. Mobile binary management and device operations are handled through specialized domain services.
strengths: Clear separation of concerns with layered architecture
Robust concurrency and async processing with Kafka
Mobile-specific domain modeling for test management
weaknesses: High coupling between layers due to numerous interdependencies
Complex module structure with potential circular dependencies
Duplicate naming (multiple models, controllers, endpoint modules)
